I'm a long long time fan, I played Fallout 1 in 1997, I played a beta of Fallout 2 in 1998, I played 3 and NV on release days. I have so far put about 10 hrs into the game.

I am having fun, and yes, I think it is worth 60$ (I got it for 75 with the season pass for preordering it, the first and last preorder of the year).

Are there things I like more about this one? Yes. Things I like less? Yes. Things I don't like at all? Yes. But I am having fun and I can't stop playing, so regardless of all of that I feel like I'm getting my money's worth. If you want the TL;DR here it is, at the beginning instead of the end.

The long version:

Things I like

  • The game runs very well for me with everything maxed out on an i7 quad 3.1 ghz with 6 gig DDR3 ram, off a SSD, with an OC GTX 960 4gb. I am using a controller and playing in 1080 on a big stupid Toshiba 40in LCD tv at 60hz.

  • It is generally stable, I have had a couple bugs but nothing game breaking. No crashes to desktop.

  • Graphically, I like the new aesthetic, so no complaints there. The enemy models and animations in particular are much much much better than Fallout 3 or even Skyrim.

  • Mechanically, the game is very similar to FO3/NV, and some of the differences are spoilers so I won't describe them in detail. I don't know how I feel about the way Power Armor is handled but I do like the new crafting system and I have no complaints (yet) about the settlement building system. Conveniently being able to build a bed and 8 boxes at the Fast Travel point makes up for a lot, in my book.

  • It actually seems like there is more to read in this one, which is good, I like lore and I've always considered additional lore a decent reward for exploration.

Things I don't like

  • The game is feels a bit too much like Fallout Effect, or Mass Fallout, whichever you prefer. The changes to conversations are awful, both making your player character speak a la Mass Effect, the selection wheel that summarizes a response with a word or two (also a la Mass Effect), skipping ahead making you say UH HUH or SURE or whatever. I don't care for the CHARACTER X DOESN'T LIKE WHAT YOU DID thing (from Dragon Age).

  • I miss my skills. I don't like having hard limits to my Perks (ie, I cant get level 4 Locksmithing until level 35 or something). It's a stupid artificial restriction and I would remove it with a mod but I don't know if that would ruin the game yet; I play the game vanilla the first time anyway.

  • Insufficient options on PC, no FOV slider, no mouse acceleration off option, and all the advanced video options are only available at the pre-game spash, not ingame. I think the last is a Gamebryo limitation but still, lame.

  • Seems like there is not enough music but maybe that's just me. Lot of repeats from FO3, that's not a bad thing at all but I'd expect more tracks if this were the case. I'm hoping there is more music later so this is a preliminary notice.

  • Despite not having any game breaking bugs there are still an awful lot of minor bugs. A lot a lot.

  • So far, the general usage of Power Armor. This might change.

  • The game just doesn't seem as... gritty as it should, I guess, but I'm still early, and I finally got the opportunity to do something 'evil' last night, so there is hope. But I don't think anyone has cursed once?

IT Outsourcing Remains Strong But Change is Coming in 2016

In 2005 my (small) company decided to outsource the IT job I did. I was a developer and took the IT part too. I spent 25% of my time on the IT part.

Big came the shock to the company when the external IT guy charged 4 times my pay for the exact same amount of time I would spend. So in the end, the company paid exactly the same, the IT guy took exactly the time I did but they lost a developer that worked 75% of the time on projects.

Also big came the realization that the outsourced IT guy would respond within 24h times, while I would already have detected the problem and resolved it a at the very moment.

A flat area has been datacenters and database administration, they have not seen an increase and there is no expectations of a future increase.

Then, just to be clear, when the author uses the term "outsourcing," s/he really means "offshoring." Because there's no practical way to move infrastructure from one location to another location without also moving the man-hours associated with that infrastructure upkeep. Even if you're paying another company to deal with the overhead, they still have to do the same amount of work with the same number of assets, so the only way that datacenters and associated personnel are seeing a falloff is that the work is being shipped off shore.

The devil is in the details...
